**Shots go where you look.** With mouselook on, a bullet that autoaim has
no target for now flies along your view instead of level, starting from your
eye, so it lands at the crosshair. Shots stop on floors and ceilings too,
leaving bullet marks and chips there. Autoaim still comes first, so fights
play as before; demos and monsters keep vanilla aiming.

**Shoot the water.** Bullets that hit a liquid throw a tall column of drops
and concentric rings that grow outward. Monsters dying in a liquid splash
where they fall, and anything wading through leaves rings behind it.
Monsters, corpses, barrels and pickups standing in a liquid sink in a
little instead of standing on top of it.

**Nukage, slime, blood and lava are thick.** They throw a few fat drops that
sit on the surface before sinking, and their rings spread slowly. They
bubble: blobs dome up and burst into specks and a small ring. Things
standing in them get a wobbling collar of goo. Water stays light, with
small quick drops that vanish back into it.

**Chunky particles.** Chips, drops, debris and rings are now solid blocks of
Doom pixels in the game's own palette, colored from the texture they come
from, moving at Doom's 35 Hz. They stay at least one pixel at any distance
and the flashlight lights them.

**Faster liquid reflections.** Only water mirrors the room now; nukage,
slime and blood no longer do. The mirrored second render also runs only when
water is actually in view, not whenever some lies nearby behind a wall.
Splashes no longer disturb the reflection.

**The top of the weapon catches lamps ahead.** A lamp ahead and above now
lights the top of the barrel, which used to stay dark.
